Regenerate with `python3 scripts/silent-sweep/d341/mkgrid.py <dir> --verify` — that generator is committed now (#1993 threw it away) and `--verify` asserts every cell it re-derives is byte-identical to the copy under scripts/silent-sweep/distilled/named/. note: WHY A NAMED SET AND NOT A DERIVED ONE. On the compiler that priced them all 56 are `loud check reject` and behave exactly like their class-mates — the derived corpus moves 0 of 1,477 classes across the whole landing and all 1,945 buildable corpus modules are `cmp` byte-identical. What names them is what the CANDIDATE did to them, which nothing reading current behaviour can see.

The landing carries the three retirement rungs instead, so all three stay LOUD. They remain in `named/` as the standing proof: strip the matching rung and each one traps again, which the ablation measured one rung at a time.
landed.price_paid: 56 cells `loud check reject` -> `check-clean INVALID WASM` (`type mismatch: expected i32, found (ref $type)`): the four scalar newtypes, `new string` and the two three-deep arrays. The checker narrows the index place; the EMITTER has no index-place narrowing channel at all — `memberPathKeyOf` is Member-shaped, `memIsNarrowed` / `memNarrowVariantIndex` only ever look at a Member receiver, and the narrowed READ arms live in `emitMem` — so the boxed element is read at the un-narrowed rep. Filed as inventory-2 D451.
